question: The name changes are confusing on this one. Some are under The Atlantic, others under The Atlantic Monthly

content.text: Does the UVA Library have a subscription to The Atlantic and do we get access to current issues?

Here's what I found for *The Atlantic*:

*Print holdings — but not current issues*
UVA holds print/microform runs at Ivy (call number `AP2.A8`), but these are listed as _By Request_ — older bound/archival volumes, not a current-issue rack. I don't see a live "current issue" record in Virgo.

• 79 vols — <https://search.lib.virginia.edu/sources/uva_library/items/u489691|Virgo record>
• 15 vols — <https://search.lib.virginia.edu/sources/uva_library/items/u719138|Virgo record>
• Microfilm — <https://search.lib.virginia.edu/sources/uva_library/items/u1684202|Virgo record>

*No dedicated digital "Atlantic" subscription found*
I didn't find a page announcing a full-text online subscription specifically to _The Atlantic_. Similar recent access programs exist for other titles:

• The New Yorker & Harper's Magazine (via Opinion Archives, free with virginia.edu login) — <https://library.virginia.edu/news/2025/access-new-yorker-and-harpers-magazine-through-uva-library|UVA Library news post>
• Time & Life magazine (full cover-to-cover issues online) — <https://www.library.virginia.edu/news/category/featured|Featured Resources>
• NYT and WSJ digital access — <https://library.virginia.edu/news/2023/access-wall-street-journal-and-new-york-times-through-uva-library|WSJ/NYT access>

*My recommendation*
Since I can't confirm a current-issue digital subscription to _The Atlantic_ from these sources, try checking the <https://guides.lib.virginia.edu/az.php|A-Z Databases> list directly or ask a librarian to confirm — some general databases like Academic Search Complete or ABI/INFORM may carry recent Atlantic articles with an embargo, even without a dedicated access page. I don't want to guess on embargo length or full-text currency without confirming.
We do have current issues - in print in Shannon Reference. We also have online access, but through aggregators as it suggested.

*The Atlantic at UVA Library*

• Current issues in print — Shannon Library, Reference section
• Online access — available through aggregator databases (not a standalone publisher subscription)
• Older bound volumes/microfilm — also held, via the Virgo records found earlier

If you'd like, I can help track down which specific aggregator database (e.g. Academic Search Complete, ProQuest, etc.) carries the full text and how far back/current the coverage goes — just let me know and I can check the <https://guides.lib.virginia.edu/az.php|A-Z Databases> listings for you.

That confusion makes sense — the magazine has literally changed its cataloged title over time.

*Why the split exists*
The Atlantic was founded in 1857 in Boston as _The Atlantic Monthly_ and used that name for well over a century before shortening it to _The Atlantic_ (per <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Atlantic|Wikipedia>). Virgo catalogs serials under the title they carried at the time, so:

*Under "The Atlantic Monthly"* (older/legacy title record)
• Darden — current print journal, `AP2 .A8` — <https://search.lib.virginia.edu/sources/uva_library/items/u2388005|Virgo record>
• Law/Klaus Reading Room — current issues (2025, 2026 shown) — <https://search.lib.virginia.edu/sources/uva_library/items/u3409988|Virgo record>
• Bound archival volumes at Ivy (By Request) and several 19th-century full-text online runs (Gale, Adam Matthew, HathiTrust, etc.)

*Under "The Atlantic"* (current title record)
• Special Collections has a copy under this title tag (`PS501.A84`, part of the Burroughs/Shoaf Collection) — <https://search.lib.virginia.edu/sources/uva_library/items/u1364033|Virgo record>
